learningObjective: Interpret Nsight Compute metrics (SM utilization, achieved occupancy, DRAM throughput, L1 hit rate) to conclude that an elementwise kernel is DRAM-bandwidth bound and choose the right mitigation.

canonicalClaims.claim: A memory-bound kernel typically shows near-peak DRAM throughput together with low SM utilization and 'long scoreboard' (memory latency) as the top warp-stall reason; adding occupancy or math cannot exceed the AI × BW ceiling — mitigation must reduce bytes moved (fusion, dtype reduction, kernel elision).
conditions: The kernel streams data with no significant reuse (elementwise, single-pass reductions).
L1/L2 hit rates are naturally low because there is no data reuse to cache.
nonImplications: Does not imply low SM utilization is always bad; for memory-bound kernels it is expected.
Does not imply that fusion is always applicable; unsupported ops or dtype boundaries can block it.

sourceMappings.locator: Speed of Light Memory Workload Analysis

misconceptions.claim: Low SM utilization always indicates an occupancy problem that can be fixed by increasing block size.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Low SM utilization can result from memory-latency stalls; the SMs are idle because they are waiting for memory, not because there are too few warps.

misconceptions.claim: L1 cache hit rate should always be maximized; higher hit rates always mean faster kernels.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For a streaming kernel with no data reuse, L1 hit rate is naturally low and does not indicate a problem; increasing SMEM allocation won't create reuse that isn't there.

misconceptions.claim: Achieved occupancy 0.85 is low; reducing register usage to reach 1.0 delivers proportional speedup.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Above ~50% occupancy, additional occupancy has diminishing returns; for memory-bound kernels, occupancy is often not the constraint at all.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA Best Practices Guide, occupancy discussion

misconceptions.claim: Adding more math per element will shift a memory-bound kernel into a compute-bound regime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only if the added math raises AI above the ridge point; a few extra FLOPs per element usually leave AI far below the ridge.

implementationFacts: Nsight Compute 'DRAM Throughput' near 100% = memory-bandwidth bound
'SM Utilization' being high requires the SMs to have work to do; memory stalls lower it
Warp stall reason 'Long Scoreboard' indicates memory latency
performanceScenarios: Elementwise activation kernels are the canonical memory-bound pattern; the standard optimization path is fusing them into the producing GEMM/conv (epilogue fusion) to eliminate the extra memory pass.
